argument: Given a proposed complete list of objects, diagonal construction changes the $n$th feature of the $n$th object to build a new object absent from the list. The schema proves uncountability, incompleteness, and multiple undecidability results by converting totality claims into self-defeating objects.
boundary: A diagonal argument requires a representation with identifiable indexed features.
The constructed object must belong to the target class; otherwise the contradiction fails.
Self-reference can be encoded indirectly through fixed-point lemmas.
